name: SparkFun Qwiic Dual Solid State Relay
description: I2C-controlled board with two TE SSRF-240D25 zero-cross solid state relays (SPST-NO, AC loads only, 12-280 VAC, 10 A with convection cooling / 25 A with forced air). An ATtiny84 running SparkFun's Qwiic Dual Solid State Relay firmware drives each relay input from 3.3 V through a transistor. Runs on 3.3 V, about 50 mA with both relays on; I2C address 0x0A (0x0B with the ADR jumper cut, or any address stored in EEPROM). Sold as: SparkFun Qwiic Dual Solid State Relay (COM-16810), 2 Qwiic connectors plus a 5-pin 0.1" header GND, 3V3, SDA, SCL, RST and a 2-way screw terminal per relay.
eli5: Two silent electronic switches for mains-powered things (lamps, heaters) that your board turns on and off over two I2C wires.

pins.name: 3V3
pins.description: Supply, 3.3 V (no regulator; feeds the ATtiny84, the I2C pull-ups and the SSR inputs, about 20 mA per relay that is on). Never 5 V: SDA/SCL are pulled up to this pin.

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: I2C data (4.7 k pull-up to 3V3 on the board, I2C jumper)

pins.name: SCL
pins.description: I2C clock (4.7 k pull-up to 3V3 on the board, I2C jumper)

pins.name: RST
pins.description: ATtiny84 reset, active low (4.7 k pull-up on the board). Leave unconnected for normal use.

supplierQuery: SparkFun Qwiic Dual Solid State Relay COM-16810
buildNotes: Commands are bytes written to 0x0A: 0x01 / 0x02 toggle relay 1 / 2, 0x0A all off, 0x0B all on. There is no per-relay on/off command: write 0x05 (relay 1) or 0x06 (relay 2) and read 1 byte (0x0F on, 0x00 off), then toggle only if needed.
Do not use the firmware's toggle-all command 0x0C: it flips the status bytes but writes the wrong ATtiny pins, so a relay can stay on while status says off. Toggle each relay instead.
Slow PWM: write 0x10 (relay 1) or 0x11 (relay 2) followed by 0-120 for an on time of n/120 of a 1 s period (0 = off). While any relay runs PWM, relays left at PWM 0 are switched off every period.
AC loads only (12-280 VAC). The SSRs are normally open; a zero-cross SSR also leaks up to 0.1 mA when off, enough to make some LED lamps glow.
10 A per relay without a fan (25 A only with forced air cooling). Use wire rated for the load current.
Mains on the screw terminals is dangerous: cut one wire of the load cable and land both ends on one relay's terminal, with the plug pulled. Keep fingers off the board while it is plugged in.
The board has 4.7 k I2C pull-ups; cut the I2C jumper if many pulled-up boards share the bus.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from qwiic_dual_ssr import QwiicDualSSR

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}))
ssr = QwiicDualSSR(i2c)  # 0x0A; 0x0B with the ADR jumper cut open
ssr.all_off()
while True:
    ssr.on(1)
    ssr.off(2)
    print('SSR1=%d SSR2=%d' % (ssr.state(1), ssr.state(2)))
    time.sleep(1)
    ssr.off(1)
    ssr.on(2)
    print('SSR1=%d SSR2=%d' % (ssr.state(1), ssr.state(2)))
    time.sleep(1)
